recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing process handoff with identity state transfer (new binary).
justification: goroutine-structure, long-running or start-up code changed: in-process patching would leave old code running in goroutines that never return; a new process starts the new goroutine structure, and the old one is drained and exits
S6 blockers (1): github.com/gotify/server/config.Get: start-up-only code already ran; its effect is baked into the live state, so patching it changes nothing
alternatives: Kubernetes rolling update (loses in-memory state, needs surge capacity)
risks: changed functions are small enough to be inlined; with S6 slot trampolines the call still dispatches through the slot, but raw binary patching (internal/livepatch) must also patch the inlining callers: github.com/gotify/server.main
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 2 functions
type information is partial (213/213 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
quiescence: old activations of main(), init-started or long-running goroutines never return, so the old process is retired by exit, not by draining; set a drain deadline in the S5 upgrader
